item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. item.title: Explore the world with Dream Yacht’s newest yachts
item.description: Embark on an adventure of a lifetime with Dream Yacht Worldwide, where the allure of distant shores meets the appeal of exciting new yacht models, freshly-delivered to our charter bases around the world. Our newest yachts are ready to take you to some of the most breathtaking destinations on the planet. From the turquoise waters of the Mediterranean to the pristine islands of the Bahamas, we’re constantly renewing our fleet with modern charter yachts from premium brands. Let’s dive into the far corners of the world and discover some of our newest additions. Fethiye, Turkey – Bali Catspace Trogir, Croatia – Lagoon 40 Exumas, Bahamas – Lagoon 46 Kotor, Montenegro – Excess 11 Naples, Italy – Lagoon 46 Cote D’Azur, France – Excess 14 Fethiye, Turkey: Sail into History with the Bali Catspace Nestled along the Turquoise Coast, Fethiye is a haven for history enthusiasts and nature lovers alike. Start your sailing vacation in Turkey from our marina in Fethiye, perfectly situated on the Gulf of Fethiye in the ‘Turkish Riviera’. A new Bali Catspace sailing catamaran will ensure comfort and convenience for your group with interior spaces and outdoor lounge areas that make it feel much larger than her 40-feet. Sail through the crystal-clear waters of Göcek Bay, where ancient Lycian tombs stand as silent sentinels. Anchor in Kapi Creek, a scenic must-visit anchorage where you can moor at the jetty to swim at the nearby beach, explore Merdivenli Cove and Seagull Bay, or hike the hills to discover ancient ruins.Then, sail to Ekincik and take a motorboat ride up the Dalyan River to the ancient city of Kaunos, where you’ll see six tombs of the kings cut into the sheer rock face. The Bali Catspace, with its innovative salon that opens fully to the outdoors, is the perfect platform for exploring this enchanting region. Whether you’re seeking adventure or relaxation, Fethiye and the Bali Catspace offer an unforgettable experience. Trogir, Croatia: Discover the Adriatic with the Lagoon 40 Start your charter in breathtaking Trogir , a UNESCO World Heritage site where you can walk through the walled city and visit gothic cathedrals. Then set sail through the picturesque islands of the Dalmatian archipelago, where ancient towns and lush vineyards await. The Lagoon 40, known for its stability and performance, is an ideal choice for exploring the dramatic Croatian coastline. Spacious outdoor areas and comfortable cabins will provide the perfect setting for a memorable vacation. Croatia’s coastline is a tapestry of natural beauty and historical significance. Visit the island of Hvar, famous for its lavender fields and vibrant nightlife. Sail to nearby Vis to discover the historic town’s stone buildings, including Garibaldi Palace, as well as its many shops and restaurants. The Lagoon 40’s efficient sail plan and modern amenities will ensure a smooth and enjoyable Croatia sailing experience for memories of a lifetime! Exumas, Bahamas: Paradise Found with the Lagoon 46 The Exumas, a string of 365 islands, is a natural paradise waiting to be explored. Sail through the brilliant turquoise waters of the Bahamas, where pristine beaches and crystal-clear lagoons await. The Lagoon 46 features a spacious interior layout and premium amenities – perfect for friends and family to enjoy this idyllic destination. The Exumas are famous for their natural wonders, including the famous swimming pigs of Big Major Cay. Staniel Cay, where you’ll find the beautiful grotto seen in the James Bond movie Thunderball, is another highlight of any Exuma yacht charter. The Lagoon 46’s larger size with spacious elevated flybridge make it ideal for groups of friends and family to enjoy an extended sailing vacation in the Exumas . Whether you’re seeking adventure or relaxation, the Exumas and the Lagoon 46 offer an unforgettable experience. item.title: Learn How to Sail: Everything You Need to Know
item.description: Whether you’re embarking on a new lifestyle on the coast or want to accomplish a new skill ahead of your next vacation, learning how to sail offers a world of adventure with friends and family. Having the knowledge to man your own boat gives you the freedom to roam the world – with the wind in your sails! If you’ve ever wanted to learn how to sail, we’ve got you covered with just about everything you need to know. Keep reading for answers to all of the essential questions, including where to start, how difficult it is and how much sailing tutelage could cost you. Want to Learn How to Sail? Here’s Everything You Need to Know. Can I Try Sailing Before Learning How to Sail Myself? Yes! Learning how to sail can be a big decision, especially if you’re planning on enrolling on a course to hone your skills or studying for certifications. There are two main ways to try out sailing before you learn how to sail: 1. Visit a Local Club for Small Boat Sailing If you want to start small, visiting your local sailing club can be a great way to try out this adventure-fuelled hobby. Most organizations offer taster sessions or discovery days, allowing you to dip your toes into the water before signing up for any serious classes. 2. Charter a Skippered Sailboat on Your Next Vacation If you’re keen to push the boat out and experience sailing like never before, why not consider chartering a skippered sailing boat on your next vacation? You’ll get the chance to watch an expert in action and get a taste for what sailing your own boat could look like. Learn more about chartering a yacht for your vacation with Dream Yacht Charter. Is It Difficult to Learn How to Sail? While controlling a masted vessel can look like an impossible task to outsiders, sailing is actually a straightforward skill to master. In fact, a skilled instructor can cover most of the basics in an afternoon and have you sailing solo in just a few days of lessons. If you want to learn how to sail a large catamaran or monohull sailing yacht, it’s worth reaching out to your local sailing school to see what kind of training is on offer. You could even sign up for a specialized course to learn how to sail a large boat while on your next vacation in a dreamy destination! Why Should I Learn How to Sail If I Don’t Own a Sailing Boat? Believe it or not, you don’t have to own your own boat in order to sail one. Instead of buying, docking and maintaining your own vessel, you can hire one locally or charter one for a relaxing vacation at sea. Simply enjoy your trip, visit the places you want to see and hand back the boat once you’re done exploring the world. Once you’re equipped with the skills you need to set sail, a bareboat yacht charter is the ideal option. Explore azure lagoons, island-hop archipelagos, experience bucket list sailing grounds and create memories with family and friends on a bareboat sailing vacation that will last a lifetime. At Dream Yacht Charter, we have 40+ destinations to choose from, including: ❖ Americas – Mexico + USA ❖ Caribbean – Antigua, Belize, British Virgin Islands + more ❖ Bahamas – Abaco + Exumas ❖ Mediterranean – Croatia, Greece, Italy + more See our full list of destinations here . How Much Does It Cost to Learn How to Sail? The amount you spend on your sailing education depends on how much it’s worth to you. If you’re planning on changing your lifestyle and making sailing a regular habit, investing more might be a wise move. If you’re just starting out and want to upskill for your first at-sea vacation, a couple of lessons should have you covered. While every school will have their own specific price list, here are some general figures: ❖ 1-2 hour lesson – under $100 ❖ Weekend / short courses – approx. $500 ❖ Vacation sailing package (including tuition, certification, accommodation, resort fees and tax) – approx. $2500-3000 Our partner, Nautilus Sailing, offers liveaboard sailing vacation packages in several amazing destinations.
